name: Gdańsk Lech Wałęsa Airport
before:
The airport for the Tricity, 12 km north west of Gdańsk and within easy reach of Sopot at 10 km and Gdynia at 23 km. It is third busiest in Poland after Warsaw and Kraków, with 7.4 million passengers in 2025.

Rail is the easy way in. The Pomeranian Metropolitan Railway runs from the airport to Wrzeszcz, into central Gdańsk and out to Gdynia Główna, connecting with the Fast Urban Railway. Buses also serve central Gdańsk, Wrzeszcz and Sopot.

The airfield is better equipped than the passenger figure suggests. The single 2,800 metre runway carries an ILS Category IIIb, which lets aircraft land in fog down to 125 metres of visibility, and the runway and taxiways use LED lighting controlled remotely from the tower. Five aprons hold up to 18 mid sized aircraft, with a separate winter de-icing pad.

Terminal T1, from 1997, has in recent years mainly handled non-Schengen flights.

The airport has been named after Lech Wałęsa, president of Poland from 1990 to 1995, since 2004.
after:
The airport for Gdańsk, Sopot and Gdynia, 12 km north west of Gdańsk, with Sopot about 10 km away and Gdynia about 23 km. It is third busiest in Poland after Warsaw and Kraków, with 7.4 million passengers in 2025.

Rail is the easy way in. Trains run to Gdańsk Wrzeszcz, where passengers change for central Gdańsk, and some continue to Sopot and Gdynia. Buses also run to central Gdańsk, Wrzeszcz and Sopot.

Its single runway is 2,800 metres long. The airport is named after Lech Wałęsa.
